title: Keep the populated build-health dashboard when a refetch fails
body:
## Summary
A failed Refresh or post-build refetch replaces the whole populated Build Health dashboard with a full-panel FetchError.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/BuildHealthDashboard/index.tsx:86 returns <FetchError> whenever `error` is set, even when a previous `report` is still in state. The loading half of this rule was fixed this round (first-load-only spinner, commit b775d70d); the error half still hides rows the user was reading. Fixed looks like: when `report` exists, render InlineErrorRetry (`@/components/modules/shared/InlineErrorRetry`, already used by PerformanceProfilingView/index.tsx:249) above the KPI row and keep the rows; FetchError stays for the no-report case. Governing: software-engineering/table (a fetch never hides rendered rows) and async-ui-states.

## Flow
- open Build Health with recorded builds
- stop the dev API or make /api/ue5-bridge/build-health 500
- click Refresh -> dashboard replaced by FetchError
- fix: branch on `error && !report` for the full-panel error; inline banner otherwise

## Expected impact
A transient API error no longer blanks the build history the user is reading. Could break: tests that assert FetchError after a refetch failure (none found by grep).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - rendered rows survive a failed refetch
Before: KPI row present after a failed refetch: 0/1 (walked from index.tsx:86 control flow).
After: predicted 1/1 with an inline retry banner.
Method: simulation - control flow walked; the deferred-fetch harness in BuildHealthDashboard.verdicts.test.tsx can reject the 2nd fetch to take the figure
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extend src/__tests__/components/evaluator/BuildHealthDashboard.verdicts.test.tsx: 2nd fetch rejects -> assert [data-stat="total-builds"] still present and a retry control exists

title: Batch Review header counts only completed modules while the bar counts all terminal ones
body:
## Summary
The Batch Review header reads "{completed}/{total} modules" while the percentage beside the bar counts completed + errored + skipped, so the two disagree on every run with an error or skip.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx:41 renders `{completed}/{total} modules`; index.tsx:30 computes pct from completed+errored+skipped (a deliberate earlier fix so the bar reaches 100%). A run with 5 completed and 5 errored shows "5/10 modules" next to "100%" and "Finished with errors". Fixed looks like one counting rule shown both places, e.g. "10/10 resolved (5 ok, 5 err)" or a header that names its denominator.

## Flow
- start Review All Modules
- some modules error or are skipped
- header 5/10 vs bar 100%

## Expected impact
Readers stop seeing two progress numbers that disagree. Could break: e2e/text assertions on the header string.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one progress rule across header and bar
Before: 5 completed + 5 errored -> header "5/10", pct "100%" (2 numbers disagree, walked from index.tsx:24-41).
After: predicted header and pct derived from the same resolved count.
Method: simulation - three batches walked (all ok: agree; 5ok/5err: disagree; 9ok/1skip: disagree)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/evaluator/BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx:30 const pct = ... ((completed + errored + skipped) / total) * 100
src/components/modules/evaluator/BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx:41 {completed}/{total} modules
instrument: render BatchReviewPanel with a mocked useBatchReview batch of 5 completed + 5 error and assert header count equals the pct numerator

title: Expose the Batch Review progress bar as a progressbar
body:
## Summary
The Batch Review progress bar is three bare divs with no role="progressbar" / aria-valuenow.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx:125-144 draws the stacked bar as plain divs. The % text sits in a sibling span with no association, and running progress is never announced. Fixed: role="progressbar" aria-valuemin=0 aria-valuemax=100 aria-valuenow={pct} aria-label="Batch review progress" on the container (ProgressRing in components/ui already does this for rings).

## Flow
- run a batch with a screen reader
- the bar is skipped; progress changes are silent
- fix: add progressbar semantics on the track div

## Expected impact
AT users can read and follow batch progress. Could break: nothing visual.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - progress reachable by AT
Before: progressbar roles in BatchReviewPanel: 0.
After: predicted 1, aria-valuenow == pct.
Method: simulation - static read of index.tsx:125; a render test is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render with a mocked batch and assert querySelector("[role=progressbar]").getAttribute("aria-valuenow") equals the displayed pct

title: Replace raw hex-alpha suffixes in the Batch Review empty state with opacity tokens
body:
## Summary
BatchReviewPanel mixes OPACITY_* tokens (header button) with raw "10"/"14"/"38" hex suffixes (empty state) on the same ACCENT colour.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx:76-78 uses `${ACCENT}${OPACITY_10}` / OPACITY_30; index.tsx:177 uses `${ACCENT}10` and index.tsx:188 `${ACCENT}14` / `${ACCENT}38`. Note `10` hex is 6% while OPACITY_10 is `1a` (10%) - the raw suffix reads like the token and is not. Fixed: withOpacity(ACCENT, OPACITY_x) at all 3 sites, choosing tokens that keep the current alpha (OPACITY_8 is deprecated-but-equal to 14).

## Flow
- grep `${ACCENT}[0-9a-f]{2}` in BatchReviewPanel -> 3 raw sites
- swap for tokens of equal value

## Expected impact
Removes a misleading near-token. No visual drift if values are matched.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - token adoption, fix-as-you-touch
Before: 3 raw hex-alpha suffix sites in BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx.
After: predicted 0.
Method: probe - grep count on the file
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/evaluator/BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx:177 style={{ backgroundColor: `${ACCENT}10` }}
src/components/modules/evaluator/BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx:188 style={{ backgroundColor: `${ACCENT}14`, color: ACCENT, border: `1px solid ${ACCENT}38` }}
instrument: grep count of `${ACCENT}` followed by two hex digits in BatchReviewPanel/index.tsx (3 -> 0)

title: Deduplicate the build-status colour function
body:
## Summary
statusColor(BuildStatus) is implemented twice with identical bodies.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/BuildHealthDashboard/helpers.ts:4 and src/components/modules/evaluator/BuildDurationTrendChart.tsx:25 both map success/failed/aborted/other to STATUS_SUCCESS/ERROR/WARNING/NEUTRAL. The chart is only rendered by BuildHealthDashboard. One rule, two copies: a status added to one (e.g. queued) silently diverges. Fixed: chart imports from BuildHealthDashboard/helpers (or helpers moves beside the chart).

## Flow
- grep "function statusColor" in src/components/modules/evaluator -> 2 build-status copies
- delete the chart copy, import the helper

## Expected impact
One place to change build-status colour. Could break: nothing; same values.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation per rule
Before: 2 implementations of the BuildStatus->colour map.
After: predicted 1.
Method: probe - grep count
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/evaluator/BuildHealthDashboard/helpers.ts:4 export function statusColor(status: BuildStatus)
src/components/modules/evaluator/BuildDurationTrendChart.tsx:25 function statusColor(status: DurationTrendPoint['status'])
instrument: grep -c "function statusColor" over the two files (2 -> 1) plus the existing BuildHealthDashboard tests green

title: Confirm before deleting a profiling capture
body:
## Summary
The trash button on a profiling capture deletes it from the server on one click, with no confirm and no undo.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/PerformanceProfilingView/SessionRail.tsx:112 calls deleteSession(row.id) directly. The capture may be the baseline (A) of a before/after compare; it is gone on a misclick beside the A/B pick buttons (24px hit targets, adjacent). The shared ui/ConfirmDialog (used in 16 component files) is the house pattern for destructive confirms.

## Flow
- pick A on a capture
- misclick the adjacent trash icon
- capture deleted, A pick silently cleared
- fix: route the click through ConfirmDialog

## Expected impact
Prevents losing a baseline capture to a misclick. Could break: SessionRail tests that click delete directly (PerformanceProfilingCompare.test.tsx would need the confirm step).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - destructive action needs consent
Before: clicks to delete a capture: 1, no confirm.
After: predicted 2 (delete + confirm), cancel leaves it.
Method: simulation - SessionRail.tsx:112 read; a render test with a mocked deleteSession is the instrument
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render SessionRail with a mocked store; click Delete -> deleteSession not called until the ConfirmDialog confirm is clicked

title: Let the CSV picker reload the same file after an edit or failed read
body:
## Summary
Re-choosing the same file in CSVImportPanel fires no change event, so a re-exported or previously failed file cannot be reloaded.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/PerformanceProfilingView/CSVImportPanel.tsx:19 handleFile never resets e.target.value, so picking the same path again is a no-op in browsers. After this round's onerror alert (commit a788db0e) tells the user to "pick the file again", that retry does nothing for the same path. Fixed: reset e.target.value = "" after reading.

## Flow
- choose capture.csv
- re-export it from UE (same path)
- choose capture.csv again -> nothing happens; stale text stays
- fix: clear the input value in handleFile

## Expected impact
Re-import of an updated capture works. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - retry path works
Before: same-path re-pick reloads: 0/1 (input value never reset).
After: predicted 1/1.
Method: simulation - browser change-event semantics; jsdom does not model same-value suppression, so the instrument is asserting the input value is cleared after a pick
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render CSVImportPanel, fire change with a File, assert the file input value is "" afterwards

title: Count CSV lines without the trailing-newline phantom
body:
## Summary
The "Loaded N lines" readout counts a trailing newline as an extra line.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/PerformanceProfilingView/CSVImportPanel.tsx:74 uses csvText.split("\n").length; a 2-row file ending in a newline reads "Loaded 3 lines". UE CSV exports end in a newline, so the figure is off by one on essentially every real import. Fixed: trim the trailing newline (and \r) before counting.

## Flow
- import "frame,ms\n1,16\n"
- readout says 3 lines
- fix: count over csvText.replace(/\r?\n$/, "")

## Expected impact
Readout matches the file. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a number on screen is true
Before: "a\nb\n" -> 3 lines (wrong).
After: predicted 2.
Method: simulation - evaluated the expression on the sample string
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: CSVImportPanel test with an OkReader returning "a\nb\n", assert "Loaded 2 lines"

title: Show the capture date, not just the time, on the profiling session rail
body:
## Summary
SessionRail labels each capture with toLocaleTimeString only, so captures from different days are indistinguishable.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/PerformanceProfilingView/SessionRail.tsx:92 renders new Date(row.importedAt).toLocaleTimeString(). The rail is the A/B picker for before/after compares; a before from yesterday at 10:02 and an after today at 10:02 read identically. Fixed: date + time (or relative time) for captures not from today.

## Flow
- import a capture on day 1 and day 2 at similar times
- rail shows two identical timestamps
- fix: include the date when not today

## Expected impact
A/B picks are unambiguous. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - picker rows are distinguishable
Before: two captures 24h apart render the same label (walked).
After: predicted distinct labels.
Method: simulation - two timestamps walked through toLocaleTimeString
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: render SessionRail with two rows 24h apart at the same clock time; assert their meta text differs

title: Route the build-health fetch failure through logger
body:
## Summary
BuildHealthDashboard logs its fetch failure with console.error instead of the repo logger.

## Description
src/components/modules/evaluator/BuildHealthDashboard/index.tsx:58 (fetchReport catch) calls console.error. ESLint permits console.error, but the convention is `logger` from @/lib/logger so the event carries the module tag and reaches the app log sink. It is the only console.* call in the context's 23 files.

## Flow
- make the build-health API fail
- error goes to the browser console only
- fix: logger.error with the projectPath

## Expected impact
Fetch failures land where the app collects logs. Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one log sink
Before: 1 console.* call in the context.
After: predicted 0.
Method: probe - grep count of console. over the 23 files
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/evaluator/BuildHealthDashboard/index.tsx:58 console.error('[BuildHealthDashboard] Failed to fetch build health:', e);
instrument: grep -c "console\." over the context file list (1 -> 0)
